questions.stem: A client with a healing pressure injury asks why the dietitian emphasized adequate protein intake. Which explanation is best?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Protein intake has no relationship to healing because collagen formation does not require amino acids","B":"Protein is used only for skeletal muscle growth and has no meaningful role in wound repair","C":"Protein should be restricted for every client with a pressure injury regardless of other conditions","D":"Protein supports tissue repair and wound healing, and significant wounds can increase protein needs"}}
questions.rationale: Adequate protein supports tissue repair, immune function, and wound healing. Nutrition plans for pressure injuries should be individualized, including consideration of increased protein needs when clinically appropriate.

questions.stem: An older adult at risk for dehydration rarely reports feeling thirsty. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Restrict routine fluids to prevent overload even when there is no clinical reason for restriction","B":"Wait until the client requests a drink because thirst remains a dependable hydration signal with age","C":"Offer fluids regularly when not contraindicated and monitor intake instead of relying only on thirst","D":"Assess hydration only once daily because frequent intake monitoring does not affect dehydration risk"}}
questions.rationale: Older adults may not reliably increase fluid intake in response to thirst. When not contraindicated, proactive access and offering of fluids plus monitoring can help reduce dehydration risk.
questions.source_detail: Older adults are disproportionately affected by dehydration partly because of reduced thirst sensation and dependence/access factors; current chapter accessed 2026-08-14.

questions.stem: After trauma, a client has significant gaps in memory for important autobiographical information that exceed ordinary forgetfulness. Which condition should be considered?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Malingering by definition, because any memory gap after trauma indicates intentional symptom production","B":"Normal forgetfulness because trauma cannot be associated with clinically important memory disruption","C":"A dissociative disorder involving disruption of memory that warrants further mental-health evaluation","D":"Antisocial personality disorder because autobiographical amnesia is a defining diagnostic feature"}}
questions.rationale: Dissociative disorders can involve disruption of memory and may be associated with trauma. A diagnosis requires clinical evaluation and exclusion of neurologic, substance-related, and other causes; the presentation should not be labeled malingering without evidence.
questions.source_detail: Clinical features: inability to recall important autobiographical information, often associated with trauma or stress, beyond ordinary forgetting; accessed 2026-08-14.

questions.stem: Which description best characterizes the traditional DSM grouping of Cluster B personality disorders?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Primary neurocognitive decline with progressive memory loss as the defining feature of the cluster","B":"Odd or eccentric patterns, including paranoid and schizoid personality disorders in the cluster","C":"Anxious or fearful patterns, including avoidant and dependent personality disorders in the cluster","D":"Dramatic, emotional, or erratic patterns, including borderline and antisocial personality disorders"}}
questions.rationale: DSM-based teaching traditionally groups antisocial, borderline, histrionic, and narcissistic personality disorders in Cluster B, often summarized as dramatic, emotional, or erratic. Cluster labels are descriptive groupings, not substitutes for individual diagnostic criteria.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Personality Disorders (Nursing: Mental Health and Community Concepts)
questions.source_detail: Current NCBI nursing text accessed 2026-08-14: Cluster B includes antisocial, borderline, histrionic, and narcissistic personality disorders and is characterized by dramatic, overly emotional, or unpredictable thinking/behavior.
